correctness.rationale: Diagonal scaling gives r=C y and the relaxed update on i gives r_i'=(1−ω)r_i, r_j'=r_j−ω c r_i. The objective decrease of a step is ω(2−ω)r_i²/2. The first-step expectations agree, so the gap is ω(2−ω)/8 times the sum over first indices i of (r_j−ω c r_i)²−(1−ω)²r_i². Expanding recovers the stated formula. The smaller eigenvalue of its bracket is (1−|c|)[2−ω(1+|c|)]; the larger is positive, and all r are attainable. This verifies equality at the threshold and both signs above it, including the no-reversal case c=0 in 0<ω<2. For c=1/2 and ω=3/2, substitution gives −9/256 and 135/256 in the two modes. κ refers only to the normalized Hessian. The supplied script was inspected, not executed; the proof and exact spot checks are independent of its finite enumeration.
